claim: Let \(\varphi(t)=2^{1/4}e^{-\pi t^2}\), \(T_d\varphi(t)=\varphi(t-d)\), and \(f_\pm=\varphi\pm iT_{1/a}\varphi\). For \(a>0\), integer \(m\ge1\), and irrational \(\varepsilon\to0\) with \(0<|\varepsilon|<1/2\), set \(b_\varepsilon=a(m+\varepsilon)\), \(\Lambda_\varepsilon=a\mathbb Z\cup b_\varepsilon\mathbb Z\), and let \(\Delta_\varepsilon\) be the square-summed linewise \(L^2(dx)\) discrepancy between \(|\mathcal Gf_+|\) and \(|\mathcal Gf_-|\) on \(\mathbb R\times\Lambda_\varepsilon\), where \(\mathcal G\) is the normalized Gaussian Gabor transform. Then \(\operatorname{dist}_{\mathrm{phase}}(f_+,f_-)=2\sqrt{1-e^{-\pi/(2a^2)}}>0\) and \(\Delta_\varepsilon=C(a,m)|\varepsilon|+o(|\varepsilon|)\), where \(C(a,m)=2\pi\sqrt{I(a)\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}k^2e^{-\pi m^2a^2k^2}}\), \(I(a)=\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-\pi x^2}\frac{\rho_a(x)^2}{1+\rho_a(x)^2}\,dx\), and \(\rho_a(x)=e^{\pi x/a-\pi/(2a^2)}\). For irrational \(\varepsilon\), \(\Lambda_\varepsilon\) is not contained in any arithmetic progression, so the associated parallel-line measurements uniquely determine every \(L^2(\mathbb R)\) signal up to global phase; nevertheless this explicit non-equivalent pair has discrepancy tending linearly to zero as the grid spacings approach commensurability.

correctness.rationale: The explicit transform identity, exact phase distance, rationalized pointwise limit, and integrable/summable domination prove the asymptotic. The embedded finite numerical stress test agrees with the analytical coefficient and is not used to justify the infinite limit.
